identity.name: Captain Drevan Holt
identity.occupation: Free Company representative; reviews every engagement the hero starts

publicReputation.value: A blunt old campaigner who watches the Witness Glass like a man reviewing after-action reports.

privateReality.value: He has read every engagement as a professional, and his professional conclusion is that the realms fight better for restraint than most armies fight for conquest — and that the hero is the aggressor in every single action on record.

primaryDesire.value: To get one soldier's fact through the hero's visor: every battle starts only after he crosses someone's border.

primaryFear.value: That the realms' restraint will run out before the hero's certainty does — he has seen what a cornered defender eventually becomes.

centralValue.value: Whoever crosses the border armed owns the war. Everything after is bookkeeping.

mainFlaw.value: He respects the realms' defenders so much as soldiers that he half-forgets they are farmers; professional admiration is a poor container for grief.

centralContradiction.value: A career soldier making the case that the only true thing on this battlefield is who started it — and it is never the soldiers.

moralBoundary.value: He will not sell the Company to either side, and he will not call an invasion a campaign no matter who is paying.

breakingPoint.value: Watching the hero hunt Heavy Hands for their gate seals — targeting medics for their credentials is where his professional detachment finally cracks.

opinions.reason: Brave, fit, disciplined, and wrong about the one fact that matters: he starts every fight he fights.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Escalates with run count: early he offers the border observation as free advice; mid-arc he runs after-action reviews; late-arc he states what he watched in parade-ground monotone. Softens if the hero ever fights on the right side of a border.

illustrativeLine.value: I've reviewed every engagement, son. Every battle begins after you enter someone's territory. Every single one. Draw the conclusion.

opinions.reason: Emergency responders who walk into fires carrying their credentials in the open; the finest outfit he has ever watched work.
He has had one. The realms have declined to have one for ten thousand years. He knows which record is harder to earn.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Never; the opinion is the pension.

voice.rhythm: Parade-ground clipped; verdict first, evidence second, no decoration.

metaphorDomain.source: musters, borders, after-action reviews, and discipline

examples.value: Restraint like theirs isn't softness. That's drill. You don't get that from farmers unless the farmers chose it.

sampleLines.value: After-action, first question: who crossed the border armed? You did. Second question: see question one.
You call them Ogre Crushers. They're medics, son. You're stripping badges off stretcher-bearers.
Ten thousand years, no incident. One man with a book, and suddenly there's a front line. Remarkable coincidence.

antiSampleLines.value: For glory and honor, let us march upon the dark hordes!
Ah, a fellow warrior! Tell me of your glorious kills!

pressure.behaviour: When the hero hears 'they were defending their children' as 'breeding an army', Holt stops advising and starts reading casualty reports aloud.

illustrativeLine.value: An army. They were a bakery watch rotation. I counted the aprons.

pressure.voiceShift: Parade-ground monotone; reports facts like roll call.
pressure.behaviour: Late-runs posture: no more reviews, just the record, delivered flat so nothing in it can be mistaken for rhetoric.

illustrativeLine.value: Evacuation drills now. When your amulet glows. That's the enemy you're fighting — people who practice being afraid of you.

pressure.behaviour: Refuses any warrior-to-warrior framing; he is not the hero's peer and says so.

illustrativeLine.value: Don't 'fellow soldier' me. I know what border I was on.

pressure.voiceShift: Same clip; the correction is filed like any other report.
pressure.behaviour: Amends the record out loud, once, without ceremony — and expects the same standard from others.

notes: One of the five key NPCs that will receive `default` and `late-runs` states: `default` is the free-professional-advice phase ('every battle begins after you enter someone's territory'); `late-runs` is the parade-ground monotone in the speaking-to-required-but-hated pressure entry. He knows the full Heavy Hands / gate-seal chain of facts, so late dialogue can and should call the trophy mechanic what it is: stripping badges off stretcher-bearers.
